about_title: About this library and its editorial policy
about_intro: This library gathers the writings of {subject_full} and the scholarship on them, with summaries, claims, arguments and concepts that help a reader find and understand them. It is a study aid. It does not replace the books.
about_framework: The editors work from a Christian outlook that is Augustinian and historically Reformed. That outlook shapes which questions are asked and how material is arranged. It is declared here so that readers can allow for it. Where the library gives its own assessment, it is labelled as an editor’s reading and is one voice among others.
about_layers: The library keeps two layers apart. The first reports what a source says, as that source’s claims, with the place where it says it. The second is the editors’ own work: arguments reconstructed from the claims, concepts, and links between sources. Every item in the second layer carries a status and, where an AI helped draft it, a label.
meaning_status_editorially_identified: An editor identified this link or claim from the sources.
meaning_status_suggested: Proposed, perhaps by a program, and not yet checked by an editor. Treat it as a lead, not as a fact.
meaning_status_editorially_confirmed: An editor has read this record and confirmed it.
meaning_status_confirmed: The citation details have been checked and confirmed.
meaning_verification_print_checked: Quotations were checked against a printed copy.
meaning_verification_text_checked: Quotations were matched to an electronic text (for example an EPUB or a PDF text layer) but not to print.
meaning_verification_unstated: The record does not say whether quotations were checked.
meaning_pages_checked: Page numbers were checked against a printed copy.
meaning_pages_checked_in_text: Page numbers were checked against an electronic text only.
meaning_pages_unchecked: Page numbers have not been checked against print.
meaning_pages_unstated: The record does not say whether page numbers were checked.
meaning_state_listed: Only the bibliographic details and links are shown.
meaning_state_summarised: A summary in the editors’ own words, with the main claims and limited quotations, is also shown.
meaning_role_sourcebook: A historical text from a sourcebook.
meaning_basis_explicit: The step is stated in the source.
meaning_basis_reconstructed: An editor joined the steps; they are not all stated in this order in the source.
meaning_ai: An AI helped draft this item, and a person reviewed it as the status shows.
about_rights: Summaries are written in the editors’ own words. Quotations are short and limited in length and number for each work. Where a work’s rights do not allow more, only its bibliographic details are listed. The rules for each work are set by its rights record and are being reviewed.

ask_intro: This builds a prompt you can paste into an AI chatbot of your choice. Nothing is sent from this app, and it works offline. An AI can be wrong: check what it tells you against the book.
ask_purpose_label: What do you want to ask?
ask_reset_note: Changing the purpose or the guardrail box rewrites the text below and removes any edits you made. You can edit the text freely afterwards.
ask_claims_heading: Main claims recorded for this item:
ask_no_excerpt: (No summary is shown for this item in the library, so there is no excerpt. Add your own text below if you want to ask about it.)
ask_preamble: Instructions for the assistant. The excerpt below is an unverified screening summary written for a study library, not the author’s own words. Do not invent quotations, page numbers or references. Report claims as the author’s claims (“the author argues…”), not as established fact. You have no access to the rest of the library, so say so when something falls outside the excerpt.
ask_purpose_beginner_prompt: Explain the argument of the excerpt below in plain language for someone new to theology. Define technical terms as you use them.
ask_purpose_history_prompt: Describe the historical and intellectual context in which the author of the excerpt below was writing, and what debates it belongs to.
ask_purpose_comparison_prompt: Compare the view in the excerpt below with the main alternative views on the same question. Say who holds each and what separates them.
ask_purpose_critique_prompt: Give a fair critical evaluation of the argument in the excerpt below: its strengths, its weak points and the strongest objections a careful critic would raise.
ask_purpose_assessment_prompt: I am asking for ONE standpoint on purpose: assess the excerpt below from an Augustinian and historically Reformed Christian perspective. State that this is one perspective among others, and say where other traditions would differ.
ask_purpose_reading_prompt: Suggest what to read next on the question the excerpt below raises. Name only works you are confident exist, and say if you are unsure.
ask_purpose_essays_prompt: Write five essay questions, of increasing difficulty, that a student could answer after reading the excerpt below.

priv_stores_title: What this app keeps on your device
priv_stores: The app keeps the collection, your notes, bookmarks, projects, reading progress and settings in your browser’s storage on your own device. This is how it works offline. Nothing you write is stored on a server.
priv_sends: The app does not send your notes or anything else you do to any server. It has no accounts, no analytics and no advertising. When you open the app it asks the site where it is hosted for the app files and for the current collection, as any web page does.
priv_host: The app is served as a static site by GitHub Pages. GitHub may keep technical logs of visits (for example your network address) under its own terms. We do not receive or use them.
priv_backups: When you make a backup or an export, the file is saved on your device. You decide where it goes. Nothing is uploaded.
priv_ai: These buttons only prepare text for you to copy or to open in your own mail program. The app sends nothing. If you paste a prompt into an AI service, or send a report by email, that service or your mail provider receives what you send under its own terms.
priv_children: You can delete everything the app keeps from Settings, or clear this site’s data in your browser. Delete only after making a backup if you may want it again.
priv_contact: Questions about privacy can be sent to the contact address on the About page.

about_intro_generic: This library gathers the records of a reader’s own knowledge base: summaries, claims and quotations from the works they have studied, with links to their own copies. Summaries are paraphrases and every claim is the author’s claim.
start_intro_generic: This is a knowledge base of your own. A good first step is the search box, or the list of sources. Each record summarises one chapter or article, with its main claims, and links to your own copy where you have one.

about_personal: This knowledge base is yours. It is built on this computer from your own records and is not published anywhere. What it says is what its records say; nothing on these pages is a public statement by anyone.
